figs.title: Sustained turn line inside the maneuver envelope
figs.caption: The stall line and n_max bound the instantaneous turn, and the corner speed gives the highest instantaneous turn rate. The sustained load factor from T = D sits lower, and the shaded band between them is where a turn bleeds energy at negative specific excess power.

figs.title: Solar aircraft day and night energy balance
figs.caption: Sunlight must cover the daytime power required plus enough charge to fly through the night. The green surplus, after charge losses, equals the red night deficit, and the battery energy swing sets the battery mass.

figs.title: Load factor around a constant speed loop
figs.caption: With constant speed and radius, L − W cos γ supplies the centripetal force, so n = V²/(gR) + cos γ. The load factor peaks at the bottom and is lowest at the top, a difference of exactly 2.

figs.title: Area rule: smoothing the total cross section
figs.caption: Wave drag depends on the total cross-sectional area distribution A(x) of the whole aircraft. Waisting the fuselage by the wing area turns the bumpy wing-body curve into one smooth Sears-Haack shape of the same volume and lowers the wave drag.

figs.title: Power required as altitude increases
figs.caption: At constant weight, the power required curve at altitude is the sea level curve with both V and P scaled by 1/√σ. The minimum power and (L/D)_max points slide out along rays through the origin, so higher altitude means faster flight for more power.
